# Project-local SDK extension

Upstream: `https://github.com/ReAI-com/reai-card-sdk`, tag `v0.0.6`, exact commit `32a1b864be3821493d6afd312aa5c8fb5a93b30f`. Copied from the already-present checkout without modifying it. Upstream `LICENSE` (MIT), manifest, README, CHANGELOG and all production `src` files are retained. Git metadata, Cargo cache, upstream examples/build outputs are not vendored.

Project-local extension date: 2026-11-09. Rustup toolchain: 1.94.0. `Cargo.toml` version remains 0.0.6; this is not represented as a new upstream SDK release. Parent crate uses this directory by explicit path and lockfile, with no global Cargo patch.

Modified upstream files:

- `src/device.rs`: wire-owned source/SD epoch and sticky terminal signal; terminal `DeviceEvent` on EOF/error/explicit disconnect; use the existing **single notification worker, command gate and inbox** for keep transfers. Observe hardware-originated recording/Wi-Fi/sync mutations synchronously before incoming/event dispatch. Incomplete keep guards and every explicit `disconnect()` clone share one retained transport cleanup task and completion watch. Dropping a waiting disconnect future does not cancel or duplicate that task; Native's retained recovery waits for the same completion before reuse. No DeviceManager replacement or second subscriber.
- `src/device/safe_transfer.rs` (new): `KeepTransferOptions` and `download_file_preserving_to`. Reuses the Lite `FILE_UPLOAD {name,keep:true}` protocol with freshly parsed main firmware >=309, ordered start/binary/end, exact expected length, absolute/idle deadlines, cancellation, and a drop guard that poisons incomplete streams and starts the shared cleanup. Absolute starts before preflight; preflight, command/incoming locks, upload command writes, writer writes and flush all select cancellation, sticky terminal, absolute and idle. Capture epoch before preflight and recheck after acquiring locks rather than absorbing observed mutations. `wait_terminal()` exposes the existing watch for Native's whole copy/durability/receipt transaction, without another notification consumer. Never calls SDK `take`.
- `src/btleplug_transport.rs`: merge matching `DeviceDisconnected` adapter events into the one NUS notification stream, including an initial connected check. This adds no scan or second NUS subscription; host compilation only, physical delivery remains for the controller to verify.
- `src/types.rs`: explicit terminal `DeviceEvent::Disconnected` (additive to the project-local Rust API).
- `src/lib.rs`: re-export `KeepTransferOptions`.
- `src/access_point.rs`: additive `download_file_to_bounded` for size limits and stream idle timeout; original download method delegates to it. Existing file deletion APIs are not enhanced or used for safe automatic deletion.

Protocol reference read locally: `ai-vibe-board` HEAD `6a0ae206b504bc71aca11b4b9807e3a088733372`, `driver-v2/src-tauri/src/dyj/link.rs:494-497,3430-3590` and `transport.rs:1-10,166-171`. Lite uses a tapped clone of a unique ordered transport because the upstream SDK does not expose keep; this extension places the keep receiver **inside** the SDK owner instead, sharing its command gate, which also prevents any raw SDK command from consuming end frames. It does not copy the whole Lite driver.

Source-retention guarantee is gated on the observed >=309 keep firmware contract. It is not inferred from a user-supplied version, Wi-Fi chip version, or a default value. Unknown/old firmware is refused before upload. No hardware experiment was performed here.

## Deletion is deliberately not invented

Upstream `DyjDevice::delete_file` sends `FILE_DELETE {filename}`; `AccessPointClient::delete_file` sends HTTP DELETE `/api/files/delete?path=...`. Neither API carries source generation/hash/lease or If-Match. FILE_DELETE may also remove matching TXT. AP/BLE list metadata includes session/seq/time/length, useful for detecting changes but not an atomic deletion precondition. Local epoch observes only received events and this host's actions; it is not a firmware-exclusive immutable lease. Therefore the bridge returns `source_retained` after repository/hash/epoch/metadata validation and sends **no deletion command**. Enabling automatic deletion requires separately verified firmware-side compare-and-delete or an exclusive immutable ownership lease; do not turn list-then-delete into a claimed transaction.

Host regression lives in the parent `src/safe_transfer_tests.rs` and `src/safe_transfer_cleanup_tests.rs`, using the real SDK parser/worker with FakeTransport. The cleanup fixture blocks only the first physical disconnect so a buggy second call would falsely permit reuse; Native must remain busy until the first completes. Writer/write-command and post-preflight gate fixtures cover terminal/cancel/idle/absolute; test-only durability faults prove zero receipts after flush/sync/rename/directory-sync failure and cancellation at receipt. No upstream Bluetooth/network test suite or physical transport was run.

## Apple notification loss guard (2026-11-09)

`Cargo.toml` selects local `../btleplug` under the Apple-only alias `btleplug_apple`; non-Apple builds retain the original registry dependency, including Android. `src/btleplug_transport.rs` uses the additive Apple fallible notification stream only for NUS, forwarding a lag error and ending instead of silently resuming a surviving suffix. The vendor retains a bounded 1024-entry notification broadcast and the complete upstream license in `../btleplug/LICENSE.md`; see its `LOCAL-EXTENSIONS.md` for provenance, memory limits and the six no-hardware Tokio regression tests. No bridge/Dart API or file protocol boundary is changed. The existing worker treats a transport error as a terminal disconnect; exposing the numeric lag count in Native task metadata would require a separate controller-owned interface change. This patch does not establish that the historic 1200-byte short read was caused by lag and does not change DFU/OTA behavior.
